title: John Reilly
content:
John Reilly

Executive Function Coach

Bachelor of Psychology

Biography

I grew up in small town Montana before moving to Missoula to give the whole college thing a go. In Missoula I obtained my first job in the social work field and immediately shifted my major to social work, and then to psychology. I ended up graduating with a Bachelor's in Psychology from the University of Montana, and will be pursuing an MSW at EWU next year.. I spent close to 6 years of my time in Missoula working as a youth counselor in a therapeutic youth home, working with a number of different clients with varying degrees of executive function concerns. I recently moved to Washington and joined the Life Skills Advocate team.

What Does Executive Functioning Mean to You?

The skills you need to process and navigate everyday life.

What Is a Strategy You Use With Clients and Use Personally?

Try to make things fun and reward yourself for hitting milestones. Trying to reach goals is often a difficult process and this can help make it feel less daunting.

How Has Your Personal Experience and Professional Development Impacted Your Coaching?

It's made me realize you're going to have setbacks and that doesn't mean you failed.

How Would You Describe Your Personal Approach to Coaching?

I try to approach everything with empathy, understanding, and humor.

Which of LSA's Core Values Resonates the Most With You, and How Do You Incorporate It With Your Clients?

Adaptive. I like seeing how we can modify different techniques or strategies to work for each individual.
author: ChrisHanson
